sources.quote: Bureau of Justice Statistics (BJS) reports show that the gap in the rate of jail incarceration between Black and White people dropped by 22% between 2011 and 2021.
sources.searcher_note: National Black/white jail-rate gap narrowed through the 2010s; same direction as the lead's 2010-2019 drop, but national aggregate, not median county.

sources.quote: the previous 10-year trend of declining racial disparities in jails may have reversed as the pandemic progressed.
sources.searcher_note: Same brief: disparity may have turned back up after 2020 (349-jail sample, 2020-2022); matches the lead's 2019-to-2023 rise.

sources.quote: The jail incarceration rate for black U.S. residents was 552 per 100,000, 3.6 times the rate for white U.S. residents (155 per 100,000) at midyear 2023
sources.searcher_note: Official national 2023 ratio 3.6x; the lead's 3.86 is a median across 356 counties, a different statistic. Publication month April 2025, day not shown.

sources.outlet: Council on Criminal Justice (hosted by Prison Policy Initiative)
sources.quote: In jails, the black-white disparity ratio dropped by 42% over the study period, falling from 6.4 to 3.8.
sources.searcher_note: National jail Black/white ratio 2000-2016 fell 6.4 to 3.8; most of the drop 2008-2016. Published December 2019, day not shown.

sources.quote: In more than half of all counties in 2019, Black people were more than twice as likely as white people to be incarcerated in jail.
sources.searcher_note: Vera's own county-level Black/white jail disparity finding for 2019, from the same Incarceration Trends data the lead re-serves; no median ratio or trend.

sources.quote: Black people are still 3.6x more likely to be incarcerated in local jails nationally than white people.
sources.searcher_note: Vera 'Divided Justice' (1990-2013 trends): Black jail rates falling, white rising; national 3.6x. Earliest source found on the declining gap.

notes: The Black/white jail disparity and its trend are widely documented: it narrowed through the 2010s (CCJ 2019, Pew 2023, Vera 2018) and may have widened after 2020 (Pew 2023). Every source gives a NATIONAL aggregate ratio (3.6x in 2023 per BJS) or a county share (Vera: over half of counties above 2x in 2019). None reports a median-county ratio over a fixed 356-county panel, the 4.57/3.41/3.86 values, or counts of counties at 10x+. A search-engine summary quoted the BJS 2023 PDF as '3.4 times ... (162 per 100,000)'; the BJS web report fetched says 3.6x (155 per 100,000), so BJS's own versions may differ. No news coverage dated after 2026-06-30 found; Vera's April 2026 release is the most recent. The Pew page returned 403 to WebFetch but loaded with curl; all quotes were checked against the raw page text.
